An array is a linear data structure where elements are stored at contiguous memory locations and are accessed using contiguous integer indices.

questions.q: The access time for element(2,4) in a 3-row, 6-column array is equal to [cite: 9]
questions.explanation: Assuming a 1-based index row-major layout, the address of element $(i, j)$ with $N$ columns is calculated as $Base + size \times ((i-1) \times N + (j-1))$. Substituting $i=2$, $j=4$, and $N=6$ yields the correct formula.

questions.q: The complexity of adding two elements to the end of an array I ... [cite: 14]
questions.explanation: Adding an element to the end of a dynamic array (with sufficient capacity) takes constant time, $O(1)$. Adding a fixed constant number of elements (like two) still operates in $O(1)$ time.

questions.q: PushBack(Key) in a single linked list without a tail is ... [cite: 17]
questions.explanation: Because there is no tail pointer, you must traverse the entire linked list from the head to find the last node before inserting, resulting in a linear time complexity of $O(n)$.

questions.q:
The correct order for the following lines in the PushBack(key) function is ...

| Step | Instruction |
|---|---|
| a | `node.next <- nil` |
| b | `node.key <- key` |
| c | `node.next <- head` |
| d | `head, tail <- node` |
| e | `if tail = nil:` |
| f | `Else:` |
| g | `tail.next <- node` |
| h | `node <- new node` |
| i | `tail <- node` | [cite: 26, 27]
questions.explanation: First, create a new node and initialize its value and next pointer (h, b, a). Next, check if the list is empty (e). If empty, set both head and tail to the new node (d). Otherwise (f), link the old tail to the new node (g) and update the tail pointer (i).
options: h, b, a, e, d, f, g, i [cite: 28]
h, b, c, e, d, f, g, i [cite: 29]
h, b, a, e, d, f, i, g [cite: 30]
h, b, a, e, d, f,  , i [cite: 31]

questions.q: Enqueue is implemented using the ............ function [cite: 32]
questions.explanation: In a queue, elements are added at the rear (Enqueue), which conceptually matches the `PushBack(key)` operation.

questions.q: In the Queue implementation with an array, the Queue is empty when ... [cite: 36]
questions.explanation: In an array-based queue (often implemented circularly), the queue is considered empty when the `read` (front) index matches the `write` (rear) index.

questions.q: The drawback of dynamic arrays is that some space is wasted. [cite: 40]
questions.explanation: To achieve $O(1)$ amortized insertion time, dynamic arrays over-allocate memory (typically doubling in size when full), leading to unused or wasted capacity.
